title: Is One Word a Rotation of the Other?

concept.title: All rotations of a word are substrings of the word written twice
body: A *rotation* of a word moves some letters from the front to the back: the rotations of `abcde` include `cdeab` and `eabcd`. Given two words `a` and `b`, decide whether `b` is a rotation of `a`. For `abcde` and `cdeab` the answer is YES; for `abcde` and `abced` it is NO. Trying every rotation and comparing costs O(n^2).

Write `a` twice: `aa = a + a`. Every rotation of `a` is a window of length `n` inside `aa`: the rotation that starts at the position `i` is `aa[i..i+n)`. So **`b` is a rotation of `a` exactly when the lengths are equal and `b` occurs as a substring of `a + a`**. The substring search can be done with the prefix function in linear time: find `b` in `a + a`.

body.code:
if len(a) != len(b): answer NO
else:
    c = b + "#" + a + a
    pi = prefix_function(c)
    answer YES if some value pi[i] == len(b) else NO

body: The length check is important: for `a = ab` and `b = b`, the word `b` occurs in `abab`, but it is not a rotation of `a`; only when the lengths agree is an occurrence a rotation. The method is linear in the length of the words. The same doubling trick finds the smallest rotation and counts the different rotations in later problems.

statement: Two words `a` and `b` are given. A rotation of a word is obtained by moving some letters (possibly none) from its start to its end. Print YES if `b` is a rotation of `a`, otherwise NO.
inputFormat: The first line has the word `a`.
The second line has the word `b`.
constraints: 1 <= length of a, length of b <= 50000
Both words consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.note: cdeab is a rotation of abcde: YES.

hints: Every rotation of a is a window of a + a.
Search b in a + a with the prefix function of b + "#" + a + a.

explanation: b is a rotation of a exactly when the lengths agree and b is a substring of a + a; the search is done with the prefix function.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def prefix_function(s):
    n = len(s)
    pi = [0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        k = pi[i - 1]
        while k and s[i] != s[k]:
            k = pi[k - 1]
        if s[i] == s[k]:
            k += 1
        pi[i] = k
    return pi

a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()

found = False
if len(a) == len(b):
    c = b + "#" + a + a
    pi = prefix_function(c)
    m = len(b)
    found = any(v == m for v in pi)
print("YES" if found else "NO")
